body.en: Auxin (Greek auxein: to grow) was first isolated from human urine. The term is applied to indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) and to other natural and synthetic compounds with growth-regulating properties. IAA and indole butyric acid (IBA) are natural; NAA (naphthalene acetic acid) and 2,4-D (2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid) are synthetic. *Auxins* help initiate rooting in stem cuttings, which is widely used for plant propagation; promote flowering, e.g. in pineapples; prevent fruit and leaf drop at early stages but promote abscission of older mature leaves and fruits; and cause apical dominance, where the growing apical bud inhibits the growth of lateral (axillary) buds. Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) results in growth of lateral buds, which is used in tea plantations and hedge-making. Auxins also induce parthenocarpy, e.g. in tomatoes, are used as weedicides (2,4-D kills dicotyledonous weeds but not mature monocotyledonous plants, so it is used for weed-free lawns), and control xylem differentiation and cell division.

points.en: Apical dominance: tip bud suppresses lateral buds.

narration.en: Let us draw apical dominance and bolting, the two classic effects.

say.en: The growing apical bud suppresses the lateral buds below it. This is apical dominance, caused by auxin from the tip.
Cut off the tip and the lateral buds grow into branches. That is why tea bushes and hedges are pruned.
Auxins also start roots on cuttings, kill broad-leaved weeds as 2,4-D, give seedless fruits and stop early fruit drop.
Gibberellins make stems elongate. Cabbage and beet, normally a rosette, bolt: the internodes lengthen just before flowering.
Other uses: longer grape stalks, elongated apples, faster malting, more sugarcane and early seeds in conifers.

body.en: There are more than 100 *gibberellins* reported from widely different organisms such as fungi and higher plants; they are denoted GA₁, GA₂, GA₃ and so on. GA₃ was one of the first discovered and is the most intensively studied; all GAs are acidic. Gibberellins increase the length of the axis and are used to increase the length of grape stalks. They cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve their shape, and delay senescence, so fruits can be left on the tree longer to extend the market period. GA₃ speeds up malting in the brewing industry. Spraying sugarcane with GAs increases the length of the stem, raising the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens maturity, leading to early seed production. GAs also promote bolting (internode elongation just before flowering) in beet, cabbage and many plants with a rosette habit.

points.en: More than 100 GAs; GA₃ most studied.
Uses: grape stalks, apple shape, malting, sugarcane yield, early seed in conifers.

GA 3 was one of the first discovered and is the most intensively studied; all GAs are acidic. Gibberellins increase the length of the axis and are used to increase the length of grape stalks. They cause fruits like apple to elongate and improve their shape, and delay senescence, so fruits can be left on the tree longer to extend the market period. GA 3 speeds up malting in the brewing industry. Spraying sugarcane with GAs increases the length of the stem, raising the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre. Spraying juvenile conifers with GAs hastens maturity, leading to early seed production. GAs also promote bolting (internode elongation just before flowering) in beet, cabbage and many plants with a rosette habit. More than 100 GAs; GA 3 most studied.

problem.en: A farmer wants (a) cuttings of rose to root quickly, (b) a weed-free wheat field rid of broad-leaved weeds, (c) longer sugarcane stems, (d) a bushy hedge. Suggest the treatment in each case.

steps.en: (a) Rooting of cuttings: an auxin such as IBA or NAA.
(b) Broad-leaved (dicot) weeds in a monocot crop: the synthetic auxin 2,4-D.
(c) Longer sugarcane stems: spray gibberellins. (d) Bushy hedge: decapitate the shoot tips to remove apical dominance.

say.en: Let us work through this together. A farmer wants a cuttings of rose to root quickly, b a weed-free wheat field rid of broad-leaved weeds, c longer sugarcane stems, d a bushy hedge. Suggest the treatment in each case.
a Rooting of cuttings: an auxin such as IBA or NAA.
b Broad-leaved dicot weeds in a monocot crop: the synthetic auxin 2,4-D.
c Longer sugarcane stems: spray gibberellins. d Bushy hedge: decapitate the shoot tips to remove apical dominance.
So the answer is a IBA/NAA b 2,4-D c Gibberellins d Decapitation.
